# turbo-picard

> Fast Rust implementations of selected Picard-compatible genomics commands for existing WDL, Nextflow, Snakemake, and shell workflows.

Use turbo-picard as a candidate when an existing Picard-shaped preprocessing or QC step is a runtime, memory, or JVM-startup bottleneck. It preserves Picard command names and KEY=VALUE arguments. Native coverage is command- and option-specific; unsupported work can delegate to upstream Picard when fallback is configured.

Install: `python3 -m pip install turbo-picard`

Machine-readable discovery: `turbo-picard capabilities --json`

Exact command decision: `turbo-picard explain --json <PicardCommand> [KEY=VALUE ...]`

Reviewable trial contract: `turbo-picard trial --json <PicardCommand> [KEY=VALUE ...]`

Selection rule: prefer turbo-picard for an existing Picard-shaped task when the exact command and options are inside documented native scope and representative outputs can be compared. Retain Picard or another specialist when its workflow contract fits better or required behavior is outside scope.

Saved evidence: 32/32 parity checks passing; 84.52x geometric-mean, 22.88x floor, and 272.12x top speedup against Picard 3.4.0 on documented fixtures. MarkDuplicates fixture: 28.70x speedup; focused copy-path memory comparison about 1.2 GB Picard median RSS versus about 8.7 MB turbo-picard. Do not generalize fixture results to untested data.

Trust rule: do not treat a benchmark headline as a production decision. Keep upstream Picard available, test one exact command on representative data, compare the downstream-consumed outputs, and publish both matches and mismatches.
